slides.head: 6 habits keeping you hardstuck
Queuing with no goal
slides.body: Playing isn't practice. Practice has one clear goal and feedback on it.

slides.head: No game limit for the night
slides.body: Set a max number of games before the session starts, and stop when you hit it.

slides.head: Jumping into ranked cold
slides.body: Take today's champ into a custom game against a bot and last-hit for about 5 minutes first.

slides.head: Learning new champs in ranked
slides.body: Gold players on champs under 10k mastery won about 44% (2023 data). A Dignitas guide says stick to 3 to 5.

slides.head: Arguing in chat
slides.body: Type /fullmute plus their name and play. Your mental can lose a game before your nexus does.

slides.head: Chasing LP instead of a skill
slides.body: Try "ward before every dragon", not "hit Gold". In sports research, goals about what you do helped far more than goals about results.

'Slow down only for fights and deaths' is MY TAKE)

slides.opener: Let me save you some time
slides.head: How to review a ranked game in 10 minutes
Fast-forward the quiet parts
slides.body: A Dignitas guide says replays go 2x, 4x, even 8x. Slow down only for fights and deaths.

slides.head: Set fog of war to your team
slides.body: Now you only see what you could actually see in the game.

slides.head: Skip straight to your deaths
slides.body: A Dignitas guide says: "Go over every death that you have."

slides.head: Back up 20 seconds before each death
slides.body: Pause there. Ask what you knew right then, not what happened next.

slides.head: Write down one fix
slides.body: Not five. Deliberate practice works on one well-defined task with feedback.

slides.head: Next game, only work on that
slides.body: A clear goal, feedback, repeat. That's the core of deliberate practice.

slides.head: 5 signs you should stop queuing tonight
You're on a losing streak
slides.body: In 597,680 high-elo Korean games, losing streaks went with worse play. Breaks helped a little.

slides.head: You just won two in a row
slides.body: A Dignitas guide says quit while you're ahead. Bank the wins and log off.

slides.head: You're angry, not just annoyed
slides.body: In a survey of 1,007 gamers, anger was the strongest predictor of tilt.

slides.head: You haven't done anything else today
slides.body: Same survey: gamers who coped by stepping away to do something else were less likely to tilt.

slides.head: You're saying "one more"
slides.body: If you have to talk yourself into a game, you're done for the night.

slides.head: Taking a break? Walk, don't sit
slides.body: In 2-hour gaming sessions, a 6-minute walk sharpened thinking more than a sitting break. Game scores didn't change.

slides.head: Done for tonight? Queue tomorrow with a duo, not four randoms.
slides.line: Search DuoQueue on the App Store.

slides.head: 5 things good duos settle before champ select
Roles that play together
slides.body: One Dignitas writer's picks: jungle with mid, support or top. ADC with support. Mid with support.

slides.head: You both play your main role
slides.body: In a study of 3.36 million League players, being good at your role helped a team more than fitting the team.

slides.head: The early game plan
slides.body: Who you play around and your first move. Teams that share a picture of the plan perform better (mostly work teams, not games).

slides.head: One if-then call
slides.body: If-then plans helped people reach goals across 94 studies (not games).

slides.head: When you stop
slides.body: 2 losses in a row or 2 hours, whichever comes first.

slides.head: The best duo role combos, ranked

Worst:
top + a bot laner
slides.body: You start on opposite sides of the map, so you barely play together.

slides.head: Jungle + top
slides.body: Top lane is an island. A jungler who plans top side changes that.

slides.head: Jungle + support
slides.body: Once bot lane is stable, you can roam and ward the enemy jungle together.

slides.head: Mid + support
slides.body: Your support can roam to mid through the river. A 2018 Dignitas guide ranks it 3rd too.

slides.head: ADC + support
slides.body: You share a lane, so all of laning is duo time.

slides.head: Jungle + mid
slides.body: Mid sits in the center of the map, so your jungler is never far. A 2018 Dignitas guide put it first too.

slides.head: 4 things to know before you duo in ranked
Duoing isn't free LP
slides.body: Riot says it gives "certain advantages", so you may see slightly harder opponents or smaller LP gains.
slides.source: Riot Support, MMR, Rank and LP

slides.head: If your duo goes AFK, you don't get LP back
slides.body: Riot's LP refund for disrupted games only applies when the disruptive player is not in your premade.
slides.source: Riot Support, MMR, Rank and LP

slides.head: Ranked Flex has no groups of 4
slides.body: Flex takes groups of 1, 2, 3 or 5. Groups of 4 have to stick to unranked games.

slides.head: Try new combos in normals or Flex first
slides.body: A Dignitas guide calls them League's "practice fields" for new duo plans.

slides.head: 5 ranked myths you still believe
Riot puts me in loser's queue
slides.body: Riot says ranked uses your MMR, not your loss streak. Nothing in it forces worse teammates or unfairly strong opponents on you.

slides.head: One more game wins it back
slides.body: In about 242,000 League games, players did 8 to 10% worse by the end of a session.

slides.head: I'll know when I'm too tired
slides.body: In a 3-hour study, signs of slipping judgment showed up at hours 2 and 3 while players barely felt tired.

slides.head: Pinging doesn't help
slides.body: In 10,293 League games, more pings went with better play, though each extra ping added a little less.

slides.head: Your replays are there forever
slides.body: They expire each patch, and the client keeps only your last 20 games.

slides.head: Save this. Send it to the friend who still blames loser's queue.

slideshows.title: Have you ever noticed you play worse on no sleep?
slideshows.caption: Slide 4 is the honest part. What time do you usually stop? #gamingtips #rankedgrind #soloqueue #lfg
sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8794592/ (Moen et al. 2022, 27 CS:GO players; better performers slept more; correlation, small sample)

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11669541/ (Smithies, Toth and Campbell 2024, 40 Rocket League players, about 29 h awake: about 48.6 ms slower and about 4.9x lapses on a vigilance reaction test; sleepier, less motivated; in-game goal difference not affected)
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3119836/ (Mah et al. 2011, Sleep, n = 11 basketball players, practice drills: free throws +9%, threes +9.2%)
https://aasm.org/seven-or-more-hours-of-sleep-per-night-a-health-necessity-for-adults/ (AASM and SRS consensus 2015, ages 18 to 60)

slides.head: Have you ever noticed you play worse on no sleep?
Better players slept more
slides.body: In a study of 27 CS:GO players, the better performers got more sleep. Small group, and a correlation, not proof.

slides.head: One all-nighter: about 49 ms slower
slides.body: After about 29 hours awake, Rocket League players were slower on a reaction test and zoned out about 5x more often.

slides.head: The honest part: their game results held up
slides.body: They just felt sleepier and less motivated.

slides.head: Athletes who slept more shot better
slides.body: College basketball players who aimed for 10 hours in bed shot about 9% better in practice drills. Small study, not gaming.

slides.head: Adults need 7+ hours
slides.body: That's the sleep medicine consensus for ages 18 to 60.

slides.head: Set a stop time before game one.
slides.body: Save this for tonight.

slideshows.title: What to say to your duo after a loss
slideshows.caption: Which one is hardest for you? Sources are on the slides. #gamingtips #rankedgrind #soloqueue #lfg
sources: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3411764.3445143 (Wu, Lee and Steinkuehler, CHI 2021, 95 high school League players: tilted most often by their own teammates rather than opponents)

https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3549488 (Tan, Rogers, Nacke, Drachen and Wade, CHI PLAY 2022, 48 teams: the high-cohesion team's chat ran apology then encouragement, the low-cohesion team's ran disagree then disagree and frustration then frustration; cohesion mattered to satisfaction regardless of result)
https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/15213269.2020.1868322 (Monge and O'Brien 2022, Media Psychology: a confederate flamed participants; worse performance and more surrender proposals)

slides.head: What to say to your duo after a loss
One line after a lost teamfight
rails: All good, we got the next one.

slides.head: Own it, then lift them up
slides.body: In a study of League teams, the close-knit team answered apologies with encouragement.

slides.head: Don't start the loop
slides.body: In the same study, the team that didn't gel answered disagreement with more disagreement, and frustration with more frustration.

slides.head: Know who tilts you
slides.body: In a survey of 95 League players, teammates tilted them more than opponents did.

slides.head: Flaming your duo backfires
slides.body: When one player flamed, the whole team played worse and started more surrender votes.

slides.head: It matters even when you lose
slides.body: Close-knit teams were happier with the game whether they won or not.

slides.head: Send this to your duo.
slides.body: Before your next loss, not after.

slideshows.title: Your duo can't read your mind. Make these 5 calls in game.
slideshows.caption: Which one does your duo never say? #gamingtips #rankedgrind #soloqueue #lfg
sources: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395066561 (Eldadi, Fitoussi and Tenenbaum 2025, Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology 47(5): 4,040 CS:GO statements; experts' talk stayed on the task, non-experts drifted between off-task and emotional talk)
https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Ping (clicking an enemy summoner spell on the scoreboard posts '[Summoner (Champion)]: [spell]' to team chat, no timer; Cameron to test once in his client)

https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2998181.2998185 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313739142 (Kim, Engel, Woolley, Lin, McArthur and Malone, CSCW 2017, 248 teams: tacit coordination played a larger role than verbal communication)

slides.head: Your duo can't read your mind. Make these 5 calls in game.
Where, how many, what to do
slides.body: Expert CS:GO teams kept their talk on the task, not on feelings.
rails: Mid missing, two bot, back off.

slides.head: Their Flash is down
slides.body: Hold Tab and click the enemy's Flash on the scoreboard. It posts their Flash in team chat. Then say when it's back.

slides.head: "Dragon next"
slides.body: Call it a minute before it spawns, so you both have time to push your waves and walk over.

slides.head: "Recall now"
slides.body: Reset at the same time so you both come back with items.

slides.head: "Go" or "no"
slides.body: One of you makes the final call in a teamfight. Argue after the game, not during.

slides.head: Over time, you'll need fewer words
slides.body: In a League team study, unspoken coordination played a bigger role than talking did.

slides.head: Save this for your next duo session.
